population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. Adults are ~268M, and 22.9% current use is ~61.4M people. Age check: 0.20×12 + 0.33×22.5 + 0.24×34.5 + 0.23×21 = 2.40 + 7.43 + 8.28 + 4.83 ≈ 22.9. Income thirds 26/23/19.5 average 22.8; the gap closed from 11 to 6.5 points because generic semaglutide, Medicaid expansion and the HRSA free programme reach the bottom third. Ever-used is 30.5% (~81.7M), so 30.5 − 22.9 = 7.6% of adults (~20.4M) have used and are off now. Cycling: ~38% of current users are restarters (0.38×22.9 ≈ 8.7 pp) and ~25% of those currently off had already cycled once (0.25×7.6 ≈ 1.9 pp), so (8.7+1.9)/30.5 ≈ 35% of ever-users have stopped and restarted. Planned 'drug holidays' of under 8 weeks are NOT counted as stops; surveys suggest ~40% of current users take at least one a year. Of the ~20.4M off-drug ever-users, ~3.5M stopped for coverage reasons (down from ~5M, because generics at $39–69 catch many who lose coverage), ~7M for side effects or intolerance, and the rest by choice, through pregnancy, or after reaching a goal. Payer mix of 61.4M current users: Medicare 14.5M (9M diabetes/cardiac/OSA/CKD-coded + 5.5M obesity-only; 65+ users ≈ 0.21×61.6M ≈ 12.9M, plus ~2M disabled under-65 beneficiaries, minus ~0.4M 65+ on retiree or cash plans); Medicaid 8M (4M diabetes-coded + 4M obesity across 34 states); HRSA free provision 2M; employer/commercial 17M; cash (brand direct and generic retail) 15M; gray market 4.9M. Sum: 14.5+8+2+17+15+4.9 = 61.4M. Public payers (24.5M, 40%) are now the largest single payer category. Never-users who would qualify clinically (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with comorbidity) and are not on a drug: still ~70M adults, mostly by choice, intolerance or disengagement rather than price. Pediatric: ~1.5% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 1.1M, of whom ~150k are aged 6–11 after the Dec 2029 liraglutide approval. About 34% of US households have at least one adult on the drug, so most children with obesity live with an on-drug adult and remain untreated themselves.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: in Jan 2030 the CMS GLP-1 Continuity Model was expanded nationally to every Part D enrollee with BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity. The CMS Chief Actuary certified the expansion as not increasing net spending once authorised-generic semaglutide was available at ~$50/month (Section 1115A(c)). Tiering: generic semaglutide first-line at $0 copay; brand tirzepatide/retatrutide at the legacy $245 rate with a ~$50 copay, after generic failure or intolerance. Conditions: ≥80% refill PDC and ≥5% loss at 6 months still apply, now with up to 4 weeks/year of clinician-documented 'planned pause' exempt from PDC, and a baseline DXA required for women ≥65 and men ≥70 since the Jun 2030 bone label. The 12-month lockout remains for brand tier; it is 3 months for generic tier. Obesity-only enrolment is 5.5M: 3.3M generic × $50 × 12 ≈ $2.0B; 2.2M brand × $245 × 12 ≈ $6.5B; total ≈ $8.5B/yr. CMS books offsetting savings from switching ~7M of the 9M diabetes-coded beneficiaries from brand (~$245 net) to generic (~$50): at full switching 7M × $195 × 12 ≈ $16.4B/yr; CMS scores ~37% of that realised in the first year ≈ $6B. Medicaid: 34 states cover obesity (up from 19), 4M enrollees; 2.8M generic × $45 × 12 ≈ $1.5B; 1.2M brand × $245 × 12 ≈ $3.5B; gross ≈ $5.0B, federal share at ~65% ≈ $3.3B. Eleven states attach adherence waivers. Children under Medicaid are covered when medically necessary under EPSDT in every state. HRSA Metabolic Health Access Program (from Apr 2030): free generic semaglutide or liraglutide at FQHCs for uninsured adults ≤250% FPL, bulk price ~$35/month; 2M enrolled by Dec 2030, an annualised run rate of 2M × $35 × 12 ≈ $0.84B against a $1.5B FY2030 appropriation (balance for clinic staffing and labs). No adherence lockout.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 70+ semaglutide brands including generic oral semaglutide at ~$6–30/month. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Southeast Asia have generic injectables at a fraction of US prices, and China's domestic semaglutide generics launched 2029–30. Tirzepatide is still brand-only almost everywhere.
access.note: Generic collapse for semaglutide only. Novo's Aug 2029 patent settlement allowed an authorised generic (Jan 2030, $69 cash) and licensed generic injectable semaglutide from Viatris, Teva, Dr. Reddy's and Sandoz from Jul 2030. By Dec 2030 retail cash is $39–59/month at Costco, Cost Plus Drugs and chain pharmacies. Brand: Wegovy/Ozempic list unchanged but direct cash cut to $129; Zepbound direct $199–249; Foundayo $99; retatrutide cut from $399 to $349 direct cash. New starts shifted back toward cheap weekly injectables (~70% of new starts), and orals fell to ~25% because generic oral semaglutide is not yet US-approved. Employer coverage for weight management rose from 44% to 49% (Business Group on Health 2030), almost entirely as generic-semaglutide-only tiers with step therapy before tirzepatide/retatrutide. BMI/adherence surcharges persist at ~1 in 5 large self-funded employers. Gray market shrank from ~6M to ~4.9M users (~8%): Indian personal imports at $15–30 still undercut US generics for the poorest, and research-peptide retatrutide/cagrilintide remains the gym-culture channel because legal retatrutide is still $349.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic brand; authorised and licensed US generics from 2030)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; brand-only)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda and generics; now labelled down to age 6)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (semaglutide, Sep 2028)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction: phase 3 AUD trial positive (Mar 2029), sNDA under review with PDUFA date Feb 2031; widely prescribed off-label now that generics cost $39–59
nicotine cessation in normal-weight smokers and vapers
semaglutide in children 6–11 (off-label; specialist-led; sNDA filed Mar 2030)
self-directed 'microdosing' and planned drug holidays to manage flatness
research-peptide retatrutide in gym and recomposition communities
drugs.pipeline_note: No new class reached the US market in 2029–30 (next_gen_launch: none). Amycretin: BLA filed Jun 2029; FDA extended the review after asking for lean-mass and bone data; decision expected mid-2031. Survodutide: filed Mar 2029; complete response letter Mar 2030 requesting DXA body-composition data in older adults; resubmission planned 2031. MariTide (monthly): phase 3 readouts 2029–30, BLA filed Oct 2030. Pediatric under-12 driver is realised through an existing product: liraglutide approved for ages 6–11 in Dec 2029 on the SCALE Kids programme (~6% BMI reduction vs placebo-arm gain at 56 weeks). Semaglutide 6–11 sNDA filed Mar 2030, under review. Semaglutide AUD sNDA filed Aug 2029 with an anhedonia (SHAPS) secondary endpoint in the label negotiation. Global incretin market ~$120B (2030): volume up sharply, US semaglutide revenue down ~60% from 2028 as generics take share.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading side-effect cause of discontinuation. Restarts after drug holidays without re-titration cause a visible spike in ER visits for vomiting and dehydration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; 2030 generic labelling adds explicit re-titration guidance after missed doses ≥2 weeks.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss and with retatrutide; cholecystectomy volumes at community hospitals up modestly.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL bellwether trials scheduled for 2031, no verdicts yet.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and sarcopenia in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a recognised population problem. Cohort DXA studies show lean tissue at ~35–40% of total loss in users ≥65, with grip-strength decline and higher fall rates in women ≥70 losing >15% of body weight.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: June 2030 class labelling update (Warnings and Precautions: loss of lean mass and bone, falls) for all incretins. Medicare requires baseline DXA for women ≥65 and men ≥70 and covers resistance-training counselling visits; professional societies recommend protein ≥1.2 g/kg and slower titration in the elderly.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: VA–Medicare linked cohort (Nov 2029, ~2.1M users): hip fracture HR ~1.3 in women ≥65 after ≥2 years of use with ≥15% weight loss, against SGLT2 comparators; absolute excess ~3 per 1,000 person-years. With ~4M women ≥65 on drug that implies roughly 10,000–12,000 excess hip and vertebral fractures a year, set against cardiovascular and diabetes benefits that remain net positive in most modelling. Signal is weaker in men and absent below 10% weight loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Dec 2029) and class label (Jun 2030); Endocrine Society guidance recommends considering antiresorptive therapy in high-risk older women on incretins. No restriction on use.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; no new decisive data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new evidence of causation, including in the AUD trial.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed from US labels (Jan 2026); not reinstated.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: First measured data: in the Mar 2029 semaglutide AUD phase 3, clinically meaningful SHAPS worsening occurred in ~11% on drug vs ~5% on placebo at 26 weeks, and was reversible on stopping. A 2030 KFF survey found 37% of current users report 'enjoying things less' at least sometimes, and 41% report adjusting dose or skipping weeks to manage it. Causality outside the AUD population is unproven.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA has asked that AUD labelling describe the SHAPS finding; label negotiation ongoing. No class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Coverage-driven stops have fallen as generics catch lapsed patients. Holiday-driven partial regain and 'yo-yo' patterns are now the common real-world case.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Underpins adherence conditions; CMS added planned-pause exemption in 2030.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More reports at retatrutide-level intake reduction and in older adults with low protein intake.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional society baseline and annual labs; incorporated into Medicare lean-mass counselling.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: 35% of ever-users have cycled, and holiday-pattern use is now widespread. The FDA Sentinel cycling study's interim report (2030) found no excess cardiometabolic harm from cycling but more GI ER visits on restart.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone accrual and growth in children under 12
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No signal in the 56-week pediatric trial, but the adult bone wave has made peak bone mass in pre-pubertal users a named unknown. About 150k children aged 6–11 are now on drug.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirement for a 5-year pediatric DXA and growth registry, attached to the Dec 2029 liraglutide approval.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~6,500 cumulatively. Growth slowed as generic semaglutide undercut compounders; research-peptide retatrutide is now the main source.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts continue; personal-importation enforcement still largely unpursued; FDA warning letters to peptide vendors.

safety_ledger.effect: Acquired olfactory and taste dysfunction (hyposmia/dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A replication in a US claims cohort (2029) found HR ~1.3. Confounding by diabetes duration is reduced but not excluded.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC concluded in 2029 with an 'uncommon' adverse reaction added to EU semaglutide and liraglutide labels; FDA review ongoing, no US label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mild and dose-related; more frequent with gray-market retatrutide dosing.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~34% of US households. Snack and confectionery unit volumes are down a further ~2–3% (≈6% below 2026) and sugary drinks ~5% below 2026. Generic pricing pulled in lower-income households, so value-tier snacks and discount-grocer categories, not only premium brands, now feel it. 'Companion' protein lines have been extended into senior and 'bone-and-muscle' nutrition (calcium, vitamin D and leucine fortification) after the June label. More private-label snack plant consolidation in Ohio and Indiana.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down another ~3–4% and beer ~2%, now with off-label AUD prescribing at $39–59 as an explicit driver in distiller guidance. On-premise bar sales outside city centres soften most. Drinks companies market 'holiday-weekend' premium products to users on planned pauses. Tobacco: US cigarette volume declines accelerate by ~1–2 points a year beyond trend; vape sales dip.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat-to-slightly-down. Half portions and small plates are standard. Casual-dining chains report 'pause-week' traffic bumps around holidays and weekends, visible in loyalty data. Buffet closures continue. Senior-dining and cafeteria contractors add protein-forward menus under hospital and Medicare Advantage wellness contracts.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting, with more Torrid and DXL closures, though the body-politics movement sustains a few direct-to-consumer brands. Rental and resale grow as households cycle sizes. Orthopedic footwear and fall-prevention products see a small senior-market bump.

fitness.state: Strength training is the growth sector. Medicare Advantage plans and the new Medicare lean-mass counselling visits funnel older users into resistance programmes, SilverSneakers-type benefits shift from cardio to weights, and physical-therapy chains open 'muscle clinics'. Big-box cardio gyms are flat.

insurance.state: Medicare and Medicaid are now the largest payers for incretins (40% of users). Employer coverage rose modestly to 49%, but as generic-only tiers; tirzepatide and retatrutide sit behind step therapy. Pharmacy trend fell to ~5% as brand semaglutide spend drops. BMI and adherence surcharges persist at ~1 in 5 large self-funded employers, now with connected-pen 'pause' flags.

pharma.state: Lilly remains dominant on tirzepatide and retatrutide, which are still brand-only. Novo traded early generic entry for royalties and tariff relief and now earns US semaglutide revenue mainly from authorised-generic and royalty streams. Generic makers (Viatris, Teva, Dr. Reddy's, Sandoz) compete to $39–59 retail. Class revenue is roughly flat in dollars on rising volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness no longer signals money; at $39 a month it signals nothing in particular. What signals class now is how a person is thin: muscled and carefully titrated versus frail and sudden. Among older women, a bone-density scan result is a new topic of conversation. 'Reta face' persists among affluent cash buyers.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The price tier has flattened and been replaced by a conditions tier. Affluent users on employer or cash brand tirzepatide/retatrutide holiday freely. Medicare and Medicaid users on generics are metered by refill data and DXA requirements. HRSA free-programme users face no lockout but get only generics. On-drug rates are 26% in the top income third and 19.5% in the bottom. Surcharges still fall on hourly workers at large self-funded employers.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: The 'pause week' has become a calendar ritual: people skip a dose before Thanksgiving, weddings, quinceañeras and cruises so they can eat and drink. Holiday tables now mix on-drug, off-drug and 'paused' guests. Church potlucks in the Mennonite, evangelical and Black church traditions remain sites of pride in eating; some congregations in Texas and Oklahoma bless food explicitly against 'the shot'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On / off / pausing' is a common dating-app field in major metros. Couples coordinate holidays around anniversaries and travel. Lower desire is now openly attributed to the drug in mainstream advice columns, and 'pause for the weekend' is common couples-therapy advice.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treatable, cheap, and now argued about out loud. Fat-liberation organisers in Oakland and Atlanta, 'Made Whole' congregations in Texas and Oklahoma, and MAHA-aligned 'natural body' influencers converge on one new target: drugs for children under 12. In Oakland and Stockton, organisers protest the HRSA clinic rollout under 'Groceries Not Shots', pointing to SNAP cuts. Their alliance stops at that issue.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Measured for the first time in the 2029 AUD trial (SHAPS worsening ~11% vs ~5% placebo). Self-reported by 37% of current users in a 2030 KFF survey ('enjoying things less at least sometimes'). Managed by 41% through dose reduction or skipped weeks. Generics at $39 make self-titration cheap, and dose-splitting from multi-dose pens is common. Still no measurement outside one indication.
interior_life.framing: Side effect with a management protocol. 'Flatness' is discussed like caffeine tolerance: a known trade-off people manage with Monday dosing (so the strongest suppression falls mid-week), lower maintenance doses and planned pauses. The 2028 framing of quieter wanting as maturity persists among AUD and smoking-cessation users.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Some employers and sales teams informally prefer Monday or Tuesday dosing so that Friday client events fall at the trough of the drug's effect. Connected-pen wellness vendors flag pauses, and surcharge disputes over 'documented pause' versus 'non-adherence' reach HR departments. Hospitality and commission-sales managers talk openly about 'flat weeks'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Comedians have a standard 'pause week' bit. Wedding planners ask guests' dosing schedules for catering counts. Bar trivia and bowling leagues keep thinning midweek and recover somewhat on holiday weekends. Musicians and writers argue publicly about whether the drug flattened their work. A few announce they are coming off it to make an album, and others credit it for being alive.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Lower desire and 'contentment over passion' are widely acknowledged. Couples therapists use anhedonia scales informally and recommend synchronised pauses. Mismatched schedules (one partner covered under Medicare rules, one on cash) produce scheduling friction rather than open conflict.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: 'Sedated workforce' rhetoric now has a number attached (the 11% figure) and is used by both the anti-pharma right and the body-liberation left. Adherence rules that punish pauses become a bipartisan grievance. CMS's 4-week planned-pause exemption is the visible concession. No measurable effect on turnout.

state.regulatory_posture: Approval-friendly but more cautious about body composition: the FDA asked for DXA data in the survodutide CRL and the amycretin review, and issued the June 2030 lean-mass/bone class label. Generic entry happened by private settlement, which the FDA processed quickly. Enforcement against personal importation and research peptides remains thin.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy: the HRSA Metabolic Health Access Program gives free generic semaglutide or liraglutide at FQHCs to uninsured adults ≤250% FPL ($1.5B FY2030 appropriation, 2M enrolled). Medicare's national Continuity Model makes generic semaglutide $0-copay first-line. Thirty-four Medicaid states cover obesity. No mandate. Pediatric under-12 coverage is effectively required in Medicaid through EPSDT when medically necessary. Oklahoma and Tennessee (2030) require two-physician sign-off and parental counselling for incretins under 12.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare: ≥80% PDC with a 4-week/year planned-pause exemption, ≥5% loss at 6 months, baseline DXA for older enrollees, 12-month lockout for brand tier and 3 months for generic. Eleven Medicaid adherence waivers, most without the pause exemption. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers run BMI/adherence surcharges with connected-pen data feeds that now distinguish 'pauses'. The HRSA programme deliberately has no adherence condition, which is its main political selling point and the main criticism from fiscal conservatives.
state.workforce_or_military: Army and Air Force accession waivers still require ≥6 months of off-drug weight stability. TRICARE added generic semaglutide for active-duty obesity under the same strict criteria. The VA, holding the largest cohort data, publishes the fracture study and adds DXA screening for older veterans on incretins.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US generic semaglutide relies largely on Indian and some Chinese API; Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs exempt generics, and the administration presents the authorised-generic deal as a tariff-relief trade with Novo. India–US price gap narrows to ~$15 vs ~$45, which shrinks the import gray market without ending it. Canada's border trade fades.

events.event: Semaglutide's phase 3 alcohol-use-disorder trial cuts heavy-drinking days versus placebo, but a secondary endpoint shows clinically meaningful anhedonia scores in 11% of treated patients against 5% on placebo; the number is everywhere within a week, and 'drug holidays' go mainstream.

Novo Nordisk settles US patent litigation with Viatris, Teva, Dr. Reddy's and Sandoz, launching an authorised generic semaglutide at $69 in January 2030 and licensing generic entry from July; by December pharmacy cash prices reach $39–59.

CMS's Chief Actuary certifies that generic pricing makes a national expansion cost-neutral, and the Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model opens to all Part D enrollees with obesity from January 2030 at a $0 generic copay, adding a 4-week planned-pause exemption; 15 more Medicaid states join by mid-2030.

FDA approves liraglutide for obesity in children aged 6 to 11, the first incretin label under 12; by spring Oklahoma and Tennessee require two-physician sign-off, and 'Made Whole' congregations and Oakland fat-liberation groups protest the same rule from opposite directions.

Congress funds a $1.5B HRSA programme giving free generic semaglutide to uninsured low-income adults at community health centres; it enrols 2 million by December, and organisers in Stockton and Oakland rally under 'Groceries Not Shots' against SNAP cuts.

After a VA–Medicare study of 2.1 million users found 30% more hip fractures among older women losing over 15% of body weight, FDA adds a class warning on muscle and bone loss to every incretin label; Medicare begins requiring baseline bone scans for older enrollees.

open_tensions: Price is no longer the barrier, so the conditions are. Medicare and Medicaid users on $0 generics are metered by refill data, DXA scans and lockouts, while affluent cash users pause at will and HRSA users face no conditions at all. The same drug carries three different freedoms.

Medicare is now the default payer for a drug class that carries a fracture warning in exactly the population Medicare covers. The cardiometabolic benefit and the hip-fracture cost are being booked by the same agency, and no one has published the net.

About 150,000 children aged 6–11 are on incretins, and their peak bone mass is a named unknown; the 5-year registry reports around 2035. Semaglutide's 6–11 filing is pending, and state laws are diverging.

Reward blunting has a number (11% vs 5%) only in alcohol-use disorder, and the AUD label due in Feb 2031 will decide whether the US label names it. Meanwhile 41% of users self-manage it with pauses that adherence rules partly punish.
still_true: Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; it has not been reinstated.
There is no US generic tirzepatide; Zepbound and Mounjaro remain brand-only under Lilly's exclusivity.
Texas's 2027 law barring BMI-based premium surcharges in state-regulated plans stands, and ERISA self-funded employer plans remain exempt.
The Army and Air Force still grant accession waivers to recruits who meet body-composition standards on a GLP-1 only after ≥6 months of off-drug weight stability.

prose.headline: Free Shot, Flat Week: The $39 Drug Is Everywhere Now, and Medicare Is Counting Your Pauses and Your Bones
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 about 61 million American adults, a little under one in four, are on an incretin drug. Price no longer explains who is on it and who is not. Novo Nordisk's patent settlement put generic semaglutide on pharmacy shelves in the summer, and by December Costco and Cost Plus sell a month of it for $39 to $59. Tirzepatide and retatrutide are still brand-only and still cost a few hundred dollars. The old drug is now as cheap as a gym membership, and so far the new ones are not.

Cheap semaglutide changed who pays. Once a month cost fifty dollars, Medicare's actuary could certify that covering everyone with obesity would not raise net spending, and the Continuity Model went national in January. Generic semaglutide is $0 for any Part D enrollee who qualifies. Brand drugs come only after the generic fails. Thirty-four states now cover obesity in Medicaid. In March, Congress funded free shots at community health centres for uninsured adults under 250 percent of the poverty line, and two million people signed up. Four in ten users now have a public payer. Employers came back a little, but most added only the generic.

The conditions matter more than the price. A Medicare user still has to refill on schedule and lose five percent in six months, and since June an older one also needs a bone scan. A Medicaid user in eleven states faces the same rules, usually without the four weeks of 'planned pause' Medicare now allows. The free-clinic user faces no rules at all, which is what its supporters like and its critics attack. A cash buyer on Zepbound answers to nobody.

The pauses are the year's habit. In March 2029 the alcohol trial reported what nobody had measured: 11 percent of treated patients scored as clinically anhedonic, against 5 percent on placebo. That turned a fringe complaint into a household one. People now talk about their 'flat week' the way they talk about jet lag. They inject on Mondays so Friday feels normal, split doses from multi-dose pens, and skip a shot before Thanksgiving, a wedding, or an anniversary. Restaurants see the skipped weeks in their loyalty data, and wedding planners ask guests about them. Employers' connected pens now have a flag that separates a pause from a lapse, and HR departments argue over which is which.

The bone problem arrived from the VA. Its linked study of two million users found hip fractures about a third more common in older women who had lost more than fifteen percent of their weight, roughly three extra per thousand per year. Across four million women that is ten thousand fractures or more annually, against cardiovascular benefits that most models still call larger. The FDA put a muscle-and-bone warning on every incretin in June. SilverSneakers classes moved from treadmills to barbells, and food companies started fortifying their protein lines with calcium.

In December 2029 liraglutide was approved for children aged six to eleven, and the backlash finally found a target it could share. Evangelical 'Made Whole' congregations in Oklahoma, fat-liberation organisers in Oakland and natural-body influencers all oppose drugging small children, though for different reasons. Oklahoma and Tennessee now require two physicians to sign off. In Stockton, protesters outside the new free clinics carry signs reading 'Groceries Not Shots', because the same Congress that funds the drug cut SNAP.

No new drug class reached the market. Two candidates stalled when the FDA asked for body-composition data. Snack and spirits volumes keep slipping, and buffets keep closing. The country is lighter and cheaper to treat. More of it is watched by its public payers, and more of it is deliberately skipping a week so it can feel something.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Héctor Salinas wakes at five in Stockton, California. The pen is in the butter compartment. It is Monday, his shot day, and he looks at it and closes the fridge.

The clinic on Airport Way gave him the pens free in May, after a nurse checked his pay stubs from the packing shed against a sheet. Nobody calls if he skips. His cousin Marisol's daughter has her quinceañera Saturday, and he wants to be hungry for it. He wants to dance without that feeling of watching himself dance from across the room.

At the shed, the conveyor runs almonds. Ruben on the next line says he paused last month for his anniversary and threw up for two days when he started again. 'Start low,' Ruben says. 'Like the paper says.'

At lunch Héctor eats a whole burrito for the first time since spring. It tastes the way burritos used to.

After work he takes Lupita, who is ten, to the pediatrician. Medi-Cal pays. The doctor shows them a chart with a curve and says the word liraglutide gently, as if it might bite. It's a daily shot. Lupita stares at the floor. 'Think about it,' the doctor says, and gives them a pamphlet with a cartoon of a girl lifting a small dumbbell.

In the car Lupita asks if it's the same as his. 'Cousin of it,' he says.

His mother calls at eight from Modesto. Medicare wants her to get a bone scan before they renew her prescription. She says she feels fine, and that her hip only hurts when it rains.

He puts the pen back behind the butter.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Some employers and sales teams informally prefer Monday or Tuesday dosing so that Friday client events fall at the trough of the drug's effect.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: weekly semaglutide has a roughly 7-day half-life and flat steady-state levels. The trough comes just before the next dose, so Friday after a Monday shot is not the trough. The 'Monday dosing so Friday feels normal' ritual, and the one-skipped-dose 'pause for the weekend', rest on pharmacology that does not support them.
